complexity.explanation: Heap sort has guaranteed O(n log n) time complexity in all cases. It uses a binary heap data structure to efficiently find the maximum element. The heap construction phase takes O(n) time, while each extraction takes O(log n) time.

description.brief: A comparison-based sorting algorithm that uses a binary heap data structure. It first builds a max heap from the input data, then repeatedly extracts the maximum element and rebuilds the heap.
detailed: • Best case:    O(n log n) - consistent performance
• Average case: O(n log n) - heap operations are logarithmic
• Worst case:   O(n log n) - guaranteed upper bound
• Optimal for systems with limited memory
• Combines advantages of merge sort and insertion sort
• Heapify: O(log n) - maintains heap property
• Extract Max: O(log n) - removes root and reheapifies
Comparison with Other O(n log n) Algorithms:
• Quick Sort: Usually faster but O(n²) worst case
• Merge Sort: Stable but requires O(n) extra space
• Heap Sort: Guaranteed O(n log n) and in-place

optimizations: Iterative heapify to avoid recursion overhead
In-place heap sort with optimized heapify
Hybrid with insertion sort for small heaps
use_cases: Real-time systems requiring guaranteed O(n log n) performance
When stable sorting is not required
Large datasets where worst-case performance matters
Systems where merge sort's memory overhead is prohibitive
disadvantages: Not stable - equal elements may change order
Poor cache performance due to non-sequential access patterns
Slower than well-implemented quicksort in practice
Not adaptive - doesn't benefit from partially sorted input
Recursive heapify may cause stack overflow for large arrays

variables.name: heap_size
variables.description: Current size of the heap (unsorted portion). Elements beyond this are already sorted.

variables.name: root
variables.description: Current root index being heapified in the heapify operation.

variables.name: largest
variables.description: Index of the largest element among root, left child, and right child during heapify.

variables.name: left
variables.description: Index of the left child in the binary heap (2*root + 1).

variables.name: right
variables.description: Index of the right child in the binary heap (2*root + 2).

variables.name: build_heap_index
variables.description: Current index during the heap construction phase.

variables.name: extract_index
variables.description: Current index during the extraction phase where max element is moved to sorted portion.

variables.name: comparisons
variables.description: Total number of element comparisons performed so far.

variables.name: swaps
variables.description: Total number of element swaps performed so far.

variables.name: phase
variables.description: Current phase of the algorithm: 'build_heap' or 'extraction'

step_types.name: Heapify Start
step_types.description: Starting heapify operation on a subtree

step_types.name: Compare Right
step_types.description: Comparing largest so far with right child

step_types.name: Swap During Heapify
step_types.description: Swapping root with larger child to maintain heap property

step_types.name: Swap Extract
step_types.description: Swapping root (max) with last element of heap

step_types.name: Extraction Complete
step_types.description: Extraction phase completed for current element

step_types.name: Completed
step_types.description: Algorithm completed - array is fully sorted
